key_insight: A smartphone-based, closed-loop interface lets users instantly identify and correct a robot policy's failure modes, enabling targeted demonstrations that improve policies far more efficiently than blind, open‑loop data collection.
problem_solved: Scales imitation learning by addressing inefficient coverage of critical states from open‑loop handheld demonstrations and reducing covariate shift without requiring the operator to be physically co-located with the robot.
method: Close the loop on handheld demonstrations: present current policy rollouts (live or replay) on a phone and let users provide targeted corrective actions where the policy fails.
Automatically incorporate corrections into the training pipeline (online or fast batch updates) so the policy improves immediately on problematic state distributions.
Lightweight mobile UI + backend that enables remote, scalable corrective data collection and rapid policy fine-tuning without extensive robot setup.
impact: Allows practitioners to collect higher-quality, targeted demonstrations at scale and iterate on robot policies faster and cheaper, improving robustness to covariate shift and reducing sample complexity for deployment.
visual_elements: Closed-loop system diagram: phone UI → policy rollout visualization → user correction → model update → robot
Before/after performance chart or heatmap showing improved state coverage and reduced failure regions
Phone UI mockup demonstrating corrective input (e.g., joystick/gesture overlay on video of robot)
Timeline/flow illustrating one-click correction to updated policy (seconds to minutes)
paper_title: RoboPocket: Improve Robot Policies Instantly with Your Phone
paper_authors: Junjie Fang, Wendi Chen, Han Xue, Fangyuan Zhou, Tian Le
